_comment: Prototype params (aging D5-b: every choice is a versioned file). Nextflow reads the same file via -params-file.

qc._rule: v1 keeps only high-res HCD with MS2 read in the Orbitrap (user, 2026-09-18)

acquisition_exception.reason: All 30 files are high-low: MS1 in the Orbitrap (FTMS + c NSI Full ms) but every one of 1,309,117 MS2 scans is IonTrap2D/HCD (ITMS + c NSI r d Full ms2 <mz>@hcd33.00) - HCD fragmentation read out in the ion trap at rapid scan rate, so fraction_orbitrap_hcd is exactly 0.0000 in every file. The deposited SDRF says Orbitrap Exploris 480, which has no ion trap and cannot emit an ITMS scan, so the instrument metadata is wrong and discovery could not have caught it (S37). MS2 counts (29,141-53,233) and run lengths (a uniform 58 min) are healthy: the acquisition is sound, it is just not the one the v1 rule allows.
acquisition_exception.rationale: Quantification reads MS1 peaks, which ARE Orbitrap here, and peptide identification from ion-trap HCD is sound - so abundance-level age effects are well founded. What low-resolution MS2 costs is fragment mass accuracy, and therefore confidence in WHERE a modification sits. This dataset is the only one in the corpus carrying donor ages (20 of 30 files, with sex), so it is the only one that can produce an age_effect row at all; admitting it for abundance and barring it from site-level PTM claims takes the part the data supports and refuses the part it does not.

search._product_mass_tolerance_why: S38. The first search of this dataset used MetaMorpheus's default ProductMassTolerance of ±20 PPM, which is a high-resolution tolerance, and every one of 39,579 matched ions in a 4,000-PSM sample fell inside ±20 ppm with a hard cutoff there - so only the small biased subset of ion-trap fragments that happened to land in a high-res window could match at all. The result was a 2.27% ID rate, a calibration failure on all 30 files, and MBR-kept exceeding MS/MS peaks. MetaMorpheus ships ProductMassTolerance_LowRes = ±0.3500 Absolute beside the default and did not select it. ±0.5 Da is the conventional ion-trap fragment tolerance and is deliberately a little looser than MetaMorpheus's own low-res value, because these are rapid-scan-rate ion-trap spectra. The precursor tolerance is NOT overridden: MS1 is Orbitrap here and the measured precursor error is tight (median -3.11 ppm, 1st-99th -4.95 to +531 ppm, the tail being isotope errors), so the default ±5 PPM is correct. This is a deviation from the pinned engine's defaults under D12 and is recorded in provenance as tolerance_overrides.

_run: PLAIN SEARCH, no Calibration and no GPTMD, at the corrected ion-trap fragment tolerance (S38; user ruling 2026-09-20). Two prior attempts with GPTMD stalled: HumanHFreducedEF_5 for >90 min and then HumanHFreducedEF_10 for >30 min, each on ~54 cores against ~7 s for every other file, and HumanHFreducedEF_10 had searched fine in the attempt before - so the stall is not a bad file and excluding files one at a time was not converging. Neither file is a bad download: both hash to the fetch manifest and their peak data matches their neighbours'. WHY DROPPING GPTMD IS RIGHT HERE RATHER THAN A SHORTCUT: D24 admits this dataset for ABUNDANCE ONLY and bars it from ptm_stoichiometry and ptm_site_localization, and GPTMD exists to discover PTMs - so the GPTMD-expanded database was buying results we are forbidden to use, at the cost of the combinatorial explosion that a 0.5 Da fragment window over ~1,000 peaks per ion-trap MS2 produces. Calibration is dropped too: it failed on all 30 files in both previous attempts (ion-trap fragments give it nothing to calibrate on). CONSEQUENCE TO CARRY LOUDLY: this dataset's counts are NOT directly comparable with PXD036557, PXD027318 or PXD032202, which were all searched Calibration -> GPTMD -> Search. It is a plain search, and its protein-group and peptide counts will be lower for that reason alone.
